candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether revenue deceleration is mainly macro/tariff/discretionary IT delay rather than churn or competitive displacement; verify retention, net revenue retention if disclosed, customer adds, ARPU, and retailer enablement program wins.
candidates.next_evidence: Read the latest 10-K, Q1 2026 earnings call, investor presentation, and customer case studies for explicit trading-partner counts, churn/retention data, revenue mix by Fulfillment/Analytics/Revenue Recovery, and mentions of Walmart, Target, Amazon, Costco, Kroger, or other anchor retailers.
candidates.node_relation: Direct operator of a retail supply-chain network connecting retailers, suppliers, grocers, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics partners through EDI, fulfillment, analytics, revenue recovery, and trading-partner connectivity.
candidates.theme_relation: A consumer-retail infrastructure toll road: if omnichannel retail, supplier onboarding, chargeback management, retailer-specific compliance, and retailer-supplier transaction complexity keep rising, the network may benefit even when visible consumer demand is mixed.
candidates.why_include: SPS is the cleanest US-listed candidate for the node. Its own 2025 10-K says recurring revenues from recurring-revenue customers were 96% of total revenue in 2025 and describes a global supply-chain network where companies connect once and can transact with thousands of trading partners. Its IR site says more than 50,000 recurring-revenue customers use SPS as their retail network. This supports the embedded operational-dependency hypothesis.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Often screened as generic vertical SaaS, small/mid-cap software, or supply-chain software, not as a consumer-retail operating network. The market may focus on decelerating 2026 revenue growth while missing that retailer-specific maps, EDI formats, compliance rules, and supplier workflows create non-contractual switching friction.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much of revenue or bookings is actually tied to retail/ecommerce/supplier networks versus broader freight, customs, and enterprise logistics; whether network volume is resilient during retail demand slowdowns.
candidates.next_evidence: Check annual report segment language, acquisition disclosures, customer case studies in retail/ecommerce, GLN transaction-volume metrics, and any disclosure around recurring revenue, gross retention, and customer concentration.

candidates.why_include: Descartes is less pure than SPS but has a plausible chokepoint role where retail transaction data touches logistics, customs, transport, and B2B messaging. Its official materials describe the Global Logistics Network as connecting hundreds of thousands of logistics, transportation, manufacturing, distribution, retail, government, and ecommerce businesses in more than 160 countries.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Usually categorized as logistics software or trade-compliance software rather than as a consumer-retail transaction dependency. The retail linkage may be buried inside customs, routing, carrier, EDI, and messaging workflows rather than visible as a consumer discretionary exposure.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether OpenText discloses Business Network/Trading Grid growth, retention, margins, transaction volumes, or customer vertical exposure; whether retail and CPG are meaningful enough to matter at the consolidated company level.
candidates.next_evidence: Review OpenText annual report, segment disclosures, product revenue growth, Trading Grid customer stories, and any management commentary on B2B integration demand, EDI-to-API migration, and retail/CPG usage.
candidates.node_relation: Diversified enterprise software company with OpenText Trading Grid, a B2B integration and EDI/API platform connecting pre-connected trading partners and supporting supply-chain information exchange.

candidates.why_underfollowed: The trading-grid asset can be hidden inside a larger, messy enterprise software conglomerate. Investors may primarily debate leverage, content-management assets, cybersecurity, or AI rather than the embedded B2B transaction-network value.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Manhattan has meaningful supplier-facing EDI, trading-partner, vendor compliance, or supplier-collaboration modules, or whether its exposure is mostly retailer-internal execution software.
candidates.next_evidence: Review product documentation, 10-K customer verticals, implementation partner materials, and case studies for supplier collaboration, EDI integrations, vendor compliance, and order/inventory workflows connecting retailers with external suppliers.

memory_update.text: SPSC should be the primary underfollowed pure-play candidate for the retail_supplier_transaction_networks node because it combines retail EDI/trading-partner workflow exposure, high recurring-revenue mix, and mid-cap size.
DSGX is a second-order adjacent candidate where the hidden exposure is B2B connectivity, customs, logistics messaging, and ecommerce/retail network data rather than pure retail EDI.
OTEX is relevant through OpenText Trading Grid but should be penalized for diluted exposure because the broader company is a diversified enterprise software platform.

The strongest falsification test for this node is whether customers can switch EDI/trading-partner networks without operational disruption; later layers should verify churn, retention, customer adds, retailer enablement wins, compliance-rule depth, and evidence of supplier complaints or retailer pushback.

Need deeper verification of private competitors and non-public infrastructure providers such as TrueCommerce, Loren Data, and other VAN/EDI providers to assess whether SPSC, DSGX, or OTEX face commoditization risk.

summary: Expanded the universe around retailer-supplier transaction networks with a deliberate bias toward underfollowed infrastructure names rather than consumer-facing ecommerce leaders. The strongest direct fit is SPS Commerce, which appears to be the purest public asset for retail EDI, trading-partner onboarding, order, invoice, shipment-notice, and compliance workflow dependency. Descartes and OpenText add adjacent B2B connectivity, logistics, customs, EDI/API, and trading-grid exposure, but with more diversified end markets. Manhattan Associates is included as a reference/adjacent leader because it embeds in retailer omnichannel, warehouse, order-management, and inventory workflows, though it is less directly a retailer-supplier transaction network.
